summary: Chesterfield County state tower; a 1944-45 state report says it was overhauled and painted, and the site record marks it removed.

facts.status_note: The Eastern US Lookouts record marks the tower as Removed. The record gives no removal date.

events.note: Overhauled and painted. The state commission report covers July 1944 to June 1945.

evidence.supports: Patrick tower is in Chesterfield County
Agency is the South Carolina Forestry Commission
Overhauled and painted in the 1944-45 report year
evidence.quote: 1944-45: The Patrick fire tower was overhauled and painted. (Report of the State Commission of Forestry, 7/1/44 to 6/30/45)

evidence.supports: Record marks the tower as removed
Most tower sites had about 10 acres, the tower and a year-round dwelling
evidence.quote: Most tower sites consisted of 10 acres of land, the tower, and a year-round dwelling for the operator.

evidence.supports: Towers were the public's point of contact for reporting fires and linked to firefighters
evidence.quote: Towers were the public's fire reporting contact point, and served as the communications link for firefighters in the field.

evidence.supports: Many early towers were built of wooden beams
evidence.quote: many of the early South Carolina towers were built from wooden beams.

evidence.supports: Every wooden tower was eventually replaced by steel
evidence.quote: Eventually, all wooden towers were replaced by steel structures.

evidence.supports: Commission closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993
evidence.quote: The Forestry Commission closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993.

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The only Patrick-specific source is the Eastern US Lookouts page, which quotes state commission reports for 1944-45. The reports were not read directly. Searches found no other Patrick source and no removal date. The story says nothing about design, height, staffing or access because no source gives them. The general system facts come from the SCFC history page, not from anything Patrick-specific.
